scale.meaning: 0 absent/unacceptable; 1 major failures; 2 meaningful revision; 3 acceptable; 4 exemplary

criteria.description: Every product, comparison, price, scarcity and first-person experience claim has support.
critical_failure_conditions: Fabricated ownership/testimonial, unverified feature or material, false equivalence to a named luxury product, or invented offer.

anchors.1: Claims changed without locating factual support.
anchors.2: Mostly supported; qualifications or scope remain ambiguous.
anchors.3: Every claim supported and qualified; no invented first-person experience.
anchors.4: Claim-to-source ledger is complete; persuasive specificity preserves every source limitation.

criteria.description: Use documented customer phrasing, objections and language patterns; reference-ad language is not customer evidence.
critical_failure_conditions: Presenting invented customer quotations as genuine.

anchors.0: No customer-language evidence or language contradicts it.
anchors.2: Some authentic phrases; obvious jargon or pasted quotes.
anchors.3: Customer phrasing and objections sound native in a fresh script.
anchors.4: Distinctive voice remains natural across hook, proof and CTA; every borrowed phrase has provenance.

criteria.description: Read the complete script aloud; assess breath groups, transitions, conversational rhythm and awkward phrasing.

anchors.1: Repeated written prose, unnatural hype or broken transitions.
anchors.3: Natural on read-through; concise speech with credible emotional progression.
anchors.4: Effortless speech, varied rhythm, specific language and no line requiring performance to disguise awkward wording.

criteria.description: Match the intended customer's situation, objection and desired outcome; demographic stereotypes are not evidence.

anchors.0: Wrong audience or incompatible purchase context.
anchors.2: Relevant audience with generic pain or outcome.
anchors.3: Specific situation and objections fit the supplied avatar evidence.
anchors.4: Precise emotional and practical relevance without stereotyping or unsupported assumptions.

criteria.description: Adapt the reference's persuasive structure to verified product truth; deliver the hook's promised payoff.
critical_failure_conditions: Bait claim that the product or script cannot support.

anchors.2: Clear angle but generic proof or weak payoff.
anchors.3: Specific hook, logical proof and earned payoff preserve relevant reference mechanics.
anchors.4: Compelling sequence with each beat earning the next and every promise resolved.

criteria.description: Use one clear, proportionate action and the actual verified offer; omit offers absent from source.
critical_failure_conditions: Invented urgency, discount, guarantee or price.

anchors.3: Clear action, accurate offer and natural transition.
anchors.4: Efficient CTA follows the audience's resolved objection without introducing friction.

scale.meaning: 0 absent/unacceptable; 1 major failures; 2 meaningful revision; 3 acceptable; 4 exemplary

criteria.description: Map every spoken line, pause and CTA to an identified shot with duration and intended audio.
critical_failure_conditions: Omitting or changing an approved claim or mandatory disclosure.

anchors.1: Several unassigned lines or contradictory timing.
anchors.3: Every line maps to a shot; totals and durations agree.
anchors.4: Shot-by-shot traceability with deliberate pacing and workable speaking duration.

criteria.description: Each B-roll shot demonstrates the nearby spoken claim or clearly serves a stated narrative purpose.
critical_failure_conditions: Wrong product/variant or shot falsely implying a product capability.

anchors.2: Mostly relevant; one or more weak matches.
anchors.3: Every B-roll shot has a precise line/claim mapping and correct product.
anchors.4: Literal demonstration and purposeful context support comprehension without redundant filler.

criteria.description: Specify reference assets and preserve shape, scale, hardware, color, material and garment/scene continuity.
critical_failure_conditions: Wrong product identity or invented feature/demo.

anchors.2: Recognizable product with unspecified important details.
anchors.3: Correct product references and continuity for all shots.
anchors.4: Specific continuity constraints cover every angle, interaction and transition.

criteria.description: Specify in/out times or frames, shot IDs, source ranges, narration spans, transition purpose and caption plan.

anchors.2: Feasible but cut intent or narration spans ambiguous.
anchors.3: Executable timing and source instructions; transitions serve the message.
anchors.4: Unambiguous cut map including handles, voice continuity and key proof moments.

criteria.description: Distinguish existing, generated and missing assets; count unique assets and generated scenes consistently.
critical_failure_conditions: Representing missing or failed media as ready.

anchors.1: Major unexplained sourcing or generation gaps.
anchors.2: Feasible with unresolved counts or dependencies.
anchors.3: Asset ledger and shot table agree; missing assets are explicit.
anchors.4: Reusable assets, constraints and dependencies are clear enough to produce without interpretation.
